data.name: One Dark Night
data.detailed_description:
Produced exclusively from real recordings of 911 calls, witness trial testimony and architectural drawings that provide the exact layout of both interiors and exteriors of the condo complex, One Dark Night tells the story of the day teenager Travyon Martin was shot and killed by neighborhood watch volunteer George Zimmerman.

By anchoring the piece in accurate and unassailable elements, the user becomes transported inside a reliable, albeit virtual, version of the story as an eyewitness. One Dark Night breaks new ground on multiple levels, including through audio carefully cleaned by forensic specialists Sourcesound and Primeau Productions, with the latter asserting that the reconstructed audio indicates George Zimmerman cocked his gun just before he gave chase.

reviews.review: One Dark Night functions not as a traditional gaming product, but as an experimental matrix of immersive virtual reality journalism, attempting to reconstruct the socio-political flashpoint of the Trayvon Martin shooting using real-world forensic components. The structural framework deliberately bypasses fictional writing and gamified objectives, anchoring its narrative vector exclusively to raw audio recordings of emergency services, trial testimonies, and exact architectural blueprints of the physical location. The design methodology utilizes spatial projection to transform the end-user from a passive consumer of information into a virtual eyewitness, leveraging spatialized audio processing to build environmental tension.From a ludological and mechanical standpoint, the software suffers from an absolute vacancy of interactive agency and traditional progression loops. The user is locked into a rigid, non-participatory layout where the interaction matrix is reduced to linear observation, resulting in immediate mechanical saturation within the initial minutes of execution. The audiovisual fidelity operates under severe generational constraints, with primitive polygon mapping and rigid asset animations breaking the immersion that the authentic forensic audio attempts to establish. This profound dichotomy between compelling real-world audio engineering and unrefined digital assets creates a persistent cognitive dissonance for the operator. Ultimately, while it serves as a polarizing manifesto for non-fiction VR documentation, it fundamentally lacks the systemic depth, optimization calibration, and ludic substance required to operate as a sustainable interactive simulation.
